Moderation of alcohol intake
Alcohol intake raises BP, particularly at an alcohol intake above approximately two drinks per day (1 oz. or 28 g of ethanol per
day). In a meta-analysis of 32 trials with 767 participants, the effects of alcohol differed by dose and time after ingestion. Low-dose
alcohol (<14 g/d) had no effect on BP. Medium-dose alcohol (14–28 g/d) lowered BP soon after ingestion, within 6 h, but did not
affect BP after 6 h. However, high-dose alcohol (>30 g/d) lowered BP within 6 h and up to 12 h later. However, after 12 h, high-
dose alcohol increased systolic BP by a mean of 3.7 mmHg and diastolic BP by a mean of 2.4 mmHg (Tasnim et al., 2020). In non-
hypertensives and hypertensives, BP reductions did not differ, potentially because of small sample sizes. In aggregate, evidence
supports recommendations to lower alcohol intake (among those who drink) as an approach to lower BP. Alcohol consumption
